youtube.title: Cloud Engineer vs DevOps Engineer: Do You Have to Choose?
youtube.description:
Cloud engineer and DevOps engineer job posts often read like the same role. Same platforms, same tools, and sometimes they are expected from the same person.

So who actually does what? We follow one startup building a video platform, from its first servers to its first broken release, and watch where each role takes over.

If you are choosing which path to learn, or reading a job post that seems to want both, start here.

instagram.body:
Same tools. Different job.

Cloud engineers and DevOps engineers both live in AWS, Docker and Terraform, which is why so many job posts blur them into one role.

Here's the split.

The cloud engineer builds the place your app runs, and answers for it. Servers, storage, networking, security, and the monthly bill.

The DevOps engineer builds the road your code takes to get there. Pipelines, tests, deploys, and the rollback when a release breaks.

In a small team, one person does both. In a bigger company, they're separate teams.

If you're choosing which to learn first, pick the problem you'd rather be paged about at 3 a.m.

The full breakdown is on YouTube, link in bio.

tiktok.body:
They're not the same job.

A cloud engineer decides where your app lives. EC2 for the servers, S3 for the videos, CloudFront to get them to viewers fast. Then keeps the bill from running away.

A DevOps engineer decides how new code gets there. Push, test, build, deploy, and roll back when a release breaks.

Both touch Terraform and Docker, and that overlap is why job posts mix them up.

Which one would you pick?
